newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. June PPI falls 0.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. June PPI falls 0.1 percent.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department reported the June Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.1 percent, and the so-called "core" rate of wholesale inflation rose 0.1 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected an unchanged reading on June PPI and a 0.1-percent increase in the core, which excludes volatile food and energy items.
DAVID BLITZER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, STANDARD AND POOR'S: "We continue to see very stable prices overall. We continue to see energy be a very good actor and hold prices down."
Speaking on Reuters Financial Television, Blitzer added: "The price picture continues to be very favorable."

KATHLEEN STEPHANSEN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, DONALDSON, LUFKIN & JENRETTE SECURITIES CORP: "A very good number. Even the intermediate and crude levels continued to show no inflation in the pipeline. It's quite extraordinary."
KEVIN FLANAGAN, VICE PRESIDENT, DEAN WITTER REYNOLDS INC: "I don't think this is enough for the (Treasury) market to break through that magical or mystical 6-1/2 percent level.
"Nonetheless, it's enough to give the market a positive tone, and ... keep alive the notion that the Fed is on hold."
Flanagan said the record sixth PPI drop suggests "the relationship between economic growth and inflation perhaps has been alterneed although I don't think it has been eliminated."
Flanagan said market reaction should be muted. "A lot of this was factored in."
DAVID JONES, VICE CHAIRMAN AND CHIEF ECONOMIST, AUBREY G. LANSTON & CO. INC: "The June PPI is still coming in better than expected.

"Six consecutive monthly declines in producer prices is really an extremely favorable inflationary report suggesting that there's not the slightest hint of inflation in the producing sector of the economy. It has been wrung out completely," Jones added.

"The core number was about in line with expecations -- a very modest 0.1 percent increase. The (Treasury) market response will be somewhat muted given the fact that the PPI report was slightly better than expected but not as shockingly positive as we've seen in some of the previous monthly figures.
"It does vindicate the Fed, particularly Chairman (Alan) Greenspan, in its decision to keep policy unchanged at the two most recent policy meetings.
"This favorable price performance leaves the Fed in a watchful, waiting stance. It suggests that the Fed can keep rates unchanged at the next policy meeting on August 19.

"The bottom line here is that the goods producing sector, because of improved productivity, cost cutting and global competition, isn't showing the slightest hint of accelerating inflation despite full employment conditions in the economy.

"The only place where we could see some inflation is in the service sector. On the consumer price sector, we might see some updrift reflecting higher hotel and airline rates. If we get inflation in this cycle, it's certainly not going to be in the goods producing sector," Jones concluded.

ASTRID ADOLFSON, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST, MCM NONEYWATCH: "(The decline) was led by petroleum prices, dropping 14.1 percent. Interestingly, some of the components (passenger cars and computer prices) were not as favorable, but they were more a function of the price drops being sharper in the prior month. The bond market should be positive, but we are seeing profit takers on every uptick."
DAN SETO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, THE NIKKO SECURITIES CO INTERNATIONAL INC: "This is a good report ... That is obviously a good inflation report for everybody.
